extracted.intended_audience: Principal Investigators and host institutions applying for ERC grants (Starting, Consolidator, Advanced, Proof of Concept) under Horizon 2020
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and evaluation criteria for preparing and submitting ERC Starting, Consolidator, Advanced and Proof of Concept grant proposals, including PI profile expectations, required proposal components, page limits, and evaluation standards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assessment of requested funding and major one-off costs
rubrics_metrics.description: As any additional funding is to cover major one-off costs it is not subject to pro-rata temporis reduction for projects of shorter duration. All funding requested is assessed during evaluation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requests for start-up costs, major equipment or access to large facilities must be justified in the proposal; evaluators will assess the funding requested against the needs of the proposed activity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consolidator Grant PI eligibility (PhD timing)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Principal Investigator shall have been awarded their first PhD over 7 and up to 12 years prior to 1 January 2016. The effective elapsed time since the award of the first PhD can be reduced in certain properly documented circumstances.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Document any eligible career breaks or circumstances (see 'Eligible Principal Investigator') to adjust the effective elapsed time.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consolidator Grant PI profile – independence & early maturity
rubrics_metrics.description: A competitive Consolidator Grant Principal Investigator must have already shown research independence and evidence of maturity, for example by having produced several important publications without the participation of their PhD supervisor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Demonstrate independent research (publications without PhD supervisor), promising early achievements appropriate to field and career stage (significant publications as main author, invited presentations, patents, awards).

rubrics_metrics.name: Early achievements track record (Consolidator) – required items
rubrics_metrics.description: In the Track Record the applicant Principal Investigator should list (if applicable): (1) Up to ten publications ... highlighting those without the presence as co-author of their PhD supervisor, and the number of citations (excluding self-citations); (2) Research monographs and any translations thereof; (3) Granted patent(s); (4) Invited presentations to peer-reviewed, internationally established conferences and/or international advanced schools; (5) Prizes/Awards/Academy memberships.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide clear bibliographic details, indicate seniority (main author) and citation counts (excluding self-citations); include other achievements where relevant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consolidator Grant PI expected time commitment
rubrics_metrics.description: Principal Investigators funded through the ERC Consolidator Grants shall spend a minimum of 50% of their total working time in an EU Member State or Associated Country and a minimum of 40% of their total working time on the ERC project.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Time commitment will be monitored; failure to meet minimum levels or levels indicated in the proposal may lead to reduction, suspension or termination of grants. Proposals proposing less than minimum percentages will be declared ineligible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Advanced Grant objective – candidate stage and expectations
rubrics_metrics.description: Advanced Grants are designed to support excellent Principal Investigators at the career stage at which they are already established research leaders with a recognised track record of research achievements. Applicant Principal Investigators must demonstrate the ground-breaking nature, ambition and feasibility of their scientific proposal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applications should evidence leadership and exceptional research achievements; lack of a significant recent record makes success unlikely.

rubrics_metrics.name: Advanced Grant maximum funding and allowable additional funding
rubrics_metrics.description: Advanced Grants may be awarded up to a maximum of EUR 2 500 000 for a period of 5 years. Up to an additional EUR 1 000 000 can be requested to cover (a) eligible 'start-up' costs for Principal Investigators moving to the EU or an Associated Country, and/or (b) the purchase of major equipment and/or (c) access to large facilities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Base maximum is pro rata reduced for shorter projects (except additional one-off funding); all requested funding is assessed during evaluation and must be justified.

rubrics_metrics.name: Advanced Grant PI profile – recent 10-year track record expectation
rubrics_metrics.description: ERC Advanced Grant Principal Investigators are expected to be active researchers and to have a track record of significant research achievements in the last 10 years which must be presented in the application. There is little prospect of an application succeeding in the absence of such a record.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Present achievements that identify you as an exceptional leader in originality and significance; match one or more benchmarks listed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Advanced Grant PI benchmarks of excellence (examples)
rubrics_metrics.description: Benchmarks include: 10 publications as senior author in major international peer-reviewed journals and/or leading field journals and proceedings; 3 major research monographs (at least one translated); international recognition through prizes/awards or academy membership; 5 granted patents; major contributions to launching careers of outstanding researchers; recognised leadership in industrial innovation; 10 invited presentations; 3 research expeditions led by applicant; organisation of 3 well-established international conferences.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Benchmarks are indicative and may be considered individually or in combination; relevance varies by field (e.g., monographs in HSS).

rubrics_metrics.name: Advanced Grant Ten-year Track Record – required list
rubrics_metrics.description: In the Track Record the applicant should list (if applicable) up to ten representative publications from the last ten years as main author (indicating citation counts excluding self-citations); research monographs and translations; granted patents; invited presentations; research expeditions led; organisation of international conferences (steering/organising committee); prizes/awards/academy memberships; major contributions to early careers of researchers; examples of leadership in industrial innovation or design.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If achievements older than ten years are relevant, they can be considered if highlighted in the CV; provide clear evidence and context.

rubrics_metrics.name: Extension of track record period for career breaks
rubrics_metrics.description: For maternity, the track record considered can be extended by 18 months for each child born before or during the last ten years. For paternity, the track record considered can be extended by the documented amount of paternity leave actually taken. For long-term illness, clinical qualification or national service the track record considered can be extended by the amount of leave actually taken and clearly explained in the career break section of the CV.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Document career breaks clearly in the CV to allow fair assessment and extension of the track record window.

rubrics_metrics.name: Advanced Grant PI expected time commitment
rubrics_metrics.description: Principal Investigators funded through the ERC Advanced Grants shall spend a minimum of 50% of their total working time in an EU Member State or Associated Country and a minimum of 30% of their total working time on the ERC project.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Time commitment will be monitored and non-compliance may lead to reduction, suspension or termination of grants. Proposals with less than the minimum percentages will be declared ineligible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Required proposal components and strict page limits
rubrics_metrics.description: A complete proposal shall consist of: Extended Synopsis (5 pages), Curriculum Vitae (2 pages), Track Record (2 pages), Scientific Proposal (15 pages), Host Institution Binding Statement of Support, Ethics Review Table, PhD record/supporting documentation (for Starting and Consolidator only). Page limits will be applied strictly; only material presented within these limits will be evaluated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Peer reviewers are not obliged to read beyond page limits; ensure all essential information is inside the stated limits. Incomplete proposals may be declared ineligible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Extended Synopsis requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: This should be a concise presentation of the full scientific proposal, with particular attention to the ground-breaking nature of the research project and the feasibility of the outlined scientific approach. At step 1 the full scientific proposal is not assessed so all essential information must be covered in the synopsis.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cover ground-breaking nature, feasibility, and ensure the synopsis stands alone for step 1 evaluation; indicate primary (and optionally secondary) evaluation panel and cross-panel nature if applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Curriculum Vitae guidance
rubrics_metrics.description: The CV should include the standard academic and research record as well as a succinct 'funding ID' specifying any current research grants and their subject, and any on-going application for work related to the proposal. Any research career gaps and/or unconventional paths should be clearly explained so that they can be fairly assessed by the evaluation panels.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide concise but complete funding and career information, and explain gaps/unconventional paths to permit fair evaluation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scientific Proposal content requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: The Scientific Proposal must describe the scientific and technical aspects, demonstrating the ground-breaking nature of the research, its potential impact and research methodology. The proposal must clearly specify the percentage of the applicant's total working time to be spent in the EU/Associated Country and on the ERC project, and provide a full estimation of the real project cost.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Methodology, feasibility, timescales and resource justification must be clear; proposing less than the minimum time commitments renders the application ineligible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Two-step evaluation procedure and step contents
rubrics_metrics.description: A single submission of the full proposal will be followed by a two-step evaluation. At step 1, the extended synopsis and the Principal Investigator's track record and CV will be assessed (and not the full scientific proposal). At step 2 the complete version of the retained proposals will be assessed (including the full scientific proposal).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure the step 1 documents contain all information needed for retention; retained proposals invited to step 2 may include interviews (Starting and Consolidator).

rubrics_metrics.name: Panel allocation, experts and exclusion requests
rubrics_metrics.description: Allocation of proposals to panels is based on applicant preference; proposals may be allocated to a different panel by agreement of Panel Chairs. Panels may request additional reviews by members of other panels or remote experts. Applicants can request up to three specific persons not to act as evaluators during submission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State panel preferences and exclusion requests during submission; exclusion permitted only if evaluation remains feasible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Excellence as sole evaluation criterion
rubrics_metrics.description: For all ERC frontier research grants, excellence is the sole criterion of evaluation. It will be applied to both: the ground-breaking nature, ambition and feasibility of the research project; and the intellectual capacity, creativity and commitment of the Principal Investigator.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluation should take account of phase of PI's transition to independence, career breaks and benchmarks; projects mainly collating existing material are unlikely to be considered 'frontier' research.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research Project evaluation elements (ground‑breaking, ambition, feasibility)
rubrics_metrics.description: To what extent does the proposed research address important challenges? To what extent are the objectives ambitious and beyond the state of the art? To what extent is the proposed research high risk/high gain?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explicitly state the challenge, novelty beyond state-of-the-art, and the risk/reward profile.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research Project evaluation: Scientific Approach and methodology
rubrics_metrics.description: To what extent is the outlined scientific approach feasible bearing in mind high risk/high gain? Is the research methodology appropriate to achieve the goals? Does the proposal involve development of novel methodology? Are proposed timescales and resources necessary and properly justified?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide feasibility evidence, methodological detail in the full Scientific Proposal, justification of timescales and resources.

rubrics_metrics.name: Principal Investigator evaluation: intellectual capacity, creativity, commitment
rubrics_metrics.description: Assessments ask: To what extent has the PI demonstrated ability to propose and conduct ground-breaking research? To what extent does the PI provide evidence of creative independent thinking? To what extent have PI achievements gone beyond the state of the art? To what extent does the PI demonstrate commitment and willingness to devote required time (minimums vary by grant type)?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For Advanced grants also assess leadership in training and advancement of young scientists; provide evidence of independence, creativity and commitment (time allocations).

rubrics_metrics.name: Outcome categories and ranking procedure
rubrics_metrics.description: At step 1 applicants will be informed: (A) is of sufficient quality to pass to step 2; (B) is of high quality but not sufficient to pass to step 2; (C) is not of sufficient quality. At step 2 applicants informed: (A) fully meets excellence and is recommended for funding; (B) meets some but not all elements and will not be funded; (C) does not meet excellence. Proposals are ranked by marks and panels' appreciation; retention to step 2 also uses a budgetary cut-off of three times the panel's indicative budget.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Successful funding depends on rank and available budget; applicants receive an evaluation report including ranking range. Restrictions on future submissions may apply based on outcomes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of plagiarism detection
rubrics_metrics.description: Plagiarism detection software may be used to analyse proposals submitted to the ERC.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure originality and proper attribution in all proposal text.

rubrics_metrics.name: Host Institution Binding Statement of Support
rubrics_metrics.description: The host institution must confirm its association with and its support to the project and the Principal Investigator by providing a binding statement that the conditions of independence are already fulfilled or will be provided to the Principal Investigator if the application is successful. Proposals that do not include this institutional statement may be declared ineligible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Obtain and include the institution's signed statement according to the provided template in Information for Applicants.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proof of Concept (PoC) eligibility and relation to ERC project
rubrics_metrics.description: PoC Grants aim to verify innovation potential of ideas arising from ERC funded projects. Eligible PIs are those of ERC frontier research projects ongoing or ended less than 12 months before the call opening. Applicants must demonstrate the relation between the PoC idea and the ERC-funded project; more than one PoC may be awarded per ERC project but only one PoC may be running at a time for the same project.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Show clear linkage to the prior ERC-funded research and that PoC activities draw substantially on that research rather than extending original research.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proof of Concept maximum size, duration and eligible costs
rubrics_metrics.description: Financial contribution up to EUR 150 000 for a period of 18 months (normally should be completed within 12 months). Reimbursement up to 100% of eligible approved direct costs and flat-rate indirect costs of 25% of total eligible direct costs. Funding requested will be judged against needs and must be fully justified.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prepare a full cost estimation and justify requested budget; extensions are exceptional.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proof of Concept proposal required elements
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposal must include: a short description of the idea and link to the ERC project; outline of the innovation potential and how PoC activities lead to commercial or social innovation; outline economic/societal impact including identification of customers and benefits, process to concrete application, IPR clarification/testing plans/partners; a reasonable plan of activities with requested resources and full cost estimation; Ethics Review table.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Focus on early-stage pre-competitive development steps, IPR strategy and contact plans with industry or end-users; justify resources and timeline within the seven-page limit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proof of Concept evaluation criteria (three criteria)
rubrics_metrics.description: PoC evaluation criteria are: (1) Excellence (Innovation potential) — Does the activity greatly help move research output towards initial steps of commercial or social innovation? (2) Impact — Are expected economic/societal benefits identified and is there a suitable process to result in a concrete application (commercialisation or generating social benefits)? (3) Quality and efficiency of the implementation — Is there a reasonable plan of activities against objectives, sound project-management including risk/contingency, qualified personnel, and a properly justified budget?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide explicit plans for analysis of distinctiveness vs existing solutions, confirmation of effectiveness, IPR strategy, and setting up contacts with industry or end-users; include risk management and demonstrate team capability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proof of Concept outcome – pass/fail and ranking
rubrics_metrics.description: Peer reviewers evaluate each eligible PoC proposal on each of the three evaluation criteria on a 'pass/fail' basis. To be considered for funding, proposals must receive a pass by a majority of peer reviewers on each of the three criteria. If budget is insufficient to fund all passing proposals, passers are ranked according to marks received, sorted by the order of the evaluation criteria; panels may meet to determine priority for ties.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure all three criteria are convincingly addressed; failure on any one leads to non-ranking and no funding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope and eligibility clarity for PoC proposals
rubrics_metrics.description: The content of the PoC proposal must relate to the objectives and the grant type set out in the call; a proposal will only be deemed ineligible on grounds of 'scope' in clear-cut cases. If doubtful, peer review may proceed pending an eligibility review; if eligibility criteria are later found unmet, the proposal will be declared ineligible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Demonstrate clear scope relation to PoC objectives and ERC-funded research; provide any required eligibility documentation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Host Institution eligibility for PoC
rubrics_metrics.description: The host institution (Applicant Legal Entity) must engage the Principal Investigator for at least the duration of the proof of concept project and must be established in a Member State or an Associated Country (or eligible international organisations/entities).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Confirm legal entity status and contractual engagement for project duration; see Annex on Associated Countries and restrictions for some third-country entities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Strict page limit for PoC proposals
rubrics_metrics.description: A strict limit of seven pages will be applied to the length of PoC proposals. Only the material presented within this limit will be evaluated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Concisely include all essential elements (innovation potential, impact, implementation plan, costs, IPR) within seven pages.
